senses: One who, or that which, diminishes something.
examples: They were also employed in coining of our money; but were accused of being likewise great clippers or diminishers of it, although strongly recommended to our Kings by the Popes, as may be supposed, for their own ends.

senses: (Of skin) wrinkled, especially in reference to the rugosity of digits soaked in water.
Resembling prunes, prune-like.
examples: The schoolmarm came to an abrupt stop in her arithmetic quizzing, her face set into a pruny scowl that looked to be permanent.

senses: A person who goes on a joyride.
Any thermosetting resin manufactured from phenols and aldehydes.
Any of a large group of pigments and flavouring agents, especially those found in grapes and wine.
A secondhand motor vehicle imported from Europe.
examples: It is interesting, nonetheless, since none of my discussions had prepared me for the price comparability of new fakes and original tokunbos, or their solid position at about two-thirds the price of new originals.

senses: A person who studies meteorology.
A weather forecaster.
Divided into compartments.
Having (a specified type of) compartments.
Arranged or groomed with a comb.
ety: From Middle English combed, kombide, equivalent to comb + -ed.

senses: The reservoir and atomizer of an e-cigarette.
ety: Blend of clear + (at)omizer, because of the transparent reservoir.
examples: RTAs are similar in design to clearomizers in that a wick transfers the liquid from the tank to the coil.

senses: The study of images and symbols as a form of communication.
ety: From icon + -ics. Compare Ancient Greek εἰκονικός (eikonikós, “relating to images”).

senses: A type of firearm cartridge where the primer is in the back rim, rather than a central primer cap. They are cheap to produce but cannot be reloaded with powder.
Possessing a theca.
A watercolour (painting)
A printed picture coloured by the application of watercolour through stencils, using a different stencil for each colour.
ety: Unadapted borrowing from French aquarelle, from obsolete Italian acquarella (“watercolour”) (later acquarello and acquerello).
examples: He looked out between whiles at the pleasant English land, an April aquarelle washed in with wondrous breadth.
He wandered about the house, looking into several rooms, and only partially at rest when he discovered Caroline in one, engaged upon some of her aquarelle sketches.

senses: Painted with frescos ("an artwork made by applying water-based pigment to wet or fresh lime mortar or plaster").
The measurement or the estimation of volume.
A chief druid.
Having antlers.
examples: Some are strangely detailed, like the hugely antlered white deer-creature-cum-forest-god seemingly stolen whole cloth from Princess Mononoke.

senses: The chief magistrate of a shire in Anglo-Saxon England.
ety: Learned borrowing from Old English ealdormann. See alderman (from Old English aldormann).

senses: That which correlates or causes correlation
A broad, flat muscle that extends behind the gastrocnemius along the back of the calf.
ety: Clipping of musculus soleus, a relative adjective to Latin solum.

senses: Any material composed of lignocellulose
An instrument or tool, such as a bodkin, for forming a loop in yarn or cord, etc.
A (usually electronic) tool for creating music loops.
Describing any artificial device that has biological components.
Any method of achieving a goal by means of a series of gradual increments, or small steps.
examples: And after a summer of extreme heat and wild weather, she evidently worries that incrementalism will not be enough to address a climate crisis that is crying out for revolution.

senses: A performer or composer of melodies.
examples: And, happy melodist, unwearied, / Forever piping songs forever new;
Debussy was the last melodist.
At the same time Mr. Elling has proved his finesse as a Hartman-like melodist, on multiple albums and many more stages.

senses: Befitting a knight; formally courteous (as a knight); chivalrous, gallant and courtly.
ety: From Middle English knyghtly, knightlich; equivalent to knight + -ly (adjectival suffix). Cognate with Old English cnihtlīċ (“boyish”), Dutch knechtelijk (“servile”), German knechtlich (“menial”).

senses: The state of being immanent; inherency.
The state of dwelling within and not extending beyond a given domain.
examples: Here the conflict between male bonding and the companionship of the transcendent quest versus sexual love and involvement in the immanence of bodily life comes right out into the open.

senses: Possessed of whiskers; covered in bristles.
examples: Michael's heavily whiskered face hadn't seen a razor in some days.
Their attention was, however, too much taken up with their fellow-passengers: a whiskered, cloaked, and cigared youth, with every thing military about him but the air:...

senses: A subheading.
A subscriber.
examples: Any book, magazine, or collection paying for cartoons. Ads: 3 lines free to subbers.

senses: A form of Japanese verse in five lines of 5, 7, 5, 7, and 7 morae.
ety: From Japanese 短歌 (tanka, “short song”), from Middle Chinese 短 (MC twanX) 歌 (MC ka) (compare Mandarin 短歌 (duǎngē) duǎngē).
examples: Like haiku, tanka is a short, classical verse form that has attracted considerable attention in this century.
One tanka poet who directly influenced Kenji is Ishikawa takuboku, who lineated tanka—an extraordinary break with the tradition of writing tanka in one line.
The notion of rhyming in Japanese tanka poetry is applied differently from what we observe in the Western poetry tradition.

senses: A person who pries.
kermes oak (Quercus coccifera)
Synonym of entheogen.
examples: The use of entheogenics declined in areas where Judaism, Christianity, and Islam were popular due to these groups' disapproval of the practice.
In spiritually inclined individuals taking entheogenics in a proper setting, this may even be easy.

senses: A prayer book containing a set order of daily prayers.

Nerium oleander, a notoriously poisonous shrub in the dogbane family, Apocynaceae, but nonetheless widely grown as an ornamental, having leathery lance-shaped leaves and deep rose-colored or white flowers.
ety: From French oléandre, from Medieval Latin oleandru, from Late Latin lorandrum, perhaps an alteration of rhododendron.

senses: One who sources something.
Related as members of a substitution class.
ety: From French paradigmatique, from Ancient Greek πᾰρᾰδειγμᾰτῐκός (părădeigmătĭkós).

senses: A fascinating person or thing.
A delicate, often frivolous head decoration worn on the hair, primarily by women.
A type of wool or lace headscarf.
examples: A more repellent personality would be hard to imagine, and yet Hedda Gabler is one of the eternal fascinators of the world stage.
Westminster Abbey was peppered with everything from neat pillbox hats to netted fascinators.

senses: In full quicken tree: the European rowan, rowan, or mountain ash (Sorbus aucuparia).
ety: From Middle English quiken (“(chiefly in place names) probably the European rowan or mountain ash (Sorbus aucuparia), and possibly also the aspen (Populus tremula), juniper (genus Juniperus, specifically the common juniper (Juniperus communis)), or service tree (Sorbus domestica)”), possibly from Old English cwician (“to bring to life, vivify; to come to life, become living; to quicken”) (see etymology 1).

senses: In the form of a distich.
